label: Reading Descartes’s causal and first-person premises
summary: Meditation III §§13–16 distinguishes the idea as a mode from its objective reality and assigns a causal demand to the latter with a degree requirement. Sections 22–27 ascribe a genuine idea of infinite substance to the finite meditator and distinguish apprehension from exhaustive comprehension and actual infinity from indefinite increase. The pinned Second Replies, AT VII 167, makes the further exclusion explicit in Proposition II’s demonstration: the objective reality of the idea of God is neither formally nor eminently contained in us.
blocker: For causal application, match every modeled representation with objective reality and bind the same content to ObjCause. For the first-person claims match the designated meditator, occurring episode and content to the frame, and show that the two excluded modes of containment exhaust InAct at its particular respect of infinity.
